title: Plasma glucagon and clinical control of maturity-onset type diabetes. Effects of diet, placebo and glipizide.

screening.rationale: Title indicates a placebo arm in a 1977 clinical trial but no abstract/full text is available to determine whether placebo/nocebo effects or responses were analyzed as the study objective rather than serving only as a control for drug efficacy.

classification.summary: Unable to determine whether placebo/nocebo effects were analyzed; reported a clinical trial comparing diet, placebo, and glipizide on plasma glucagon and clinical control in adults with maturity-onset diabetes.

title: Placebos in dentistry: their profound potential effects.
journal: Journal of the American Dental Association (1939)
abstract: The placebo effect may influence the treatment of patients with postextraction pain, localized osteitis, and myofascial pain dysfunction syndrome, to name a few. The patient, the doctor, and the situation all influence the placebo effect. This phenomenon is still not understood, and further research is needed. The practitioner should learn to utilize the placebo effect for its potential benefits.

screening.rationale: Narrative article whose main subject was the placebo effect in dentistry and recommendations for clinical use, fitting 'placebo science more broadly' inclusion criterion.

classification.summary: Discussed the influence and potential clinical utility of placebo effects in dental conditions (postextraction pain, osteitis, myofascial pain) and called for more research and practitioner awareness.

title: Acupuncture analgesia. I. Review of clinical studies.
journal: Australian and New Zealand journal of medicine
abstract: Recent clinical studies, both uncontrolled and controlled, of the use of acupuncture for the relief of chronic pain are reviewed. The success rate demonstrated by controlled trials is markedly lower than that claimed in reports of the clinical use of acupuncture in which no attempt is made to control factors which influence the placebo response. Although on balance of evidence it appears that acupuncture has a place in the management of chronic pain resistant to orthodox therapeutic measures, more research is needed both to establish objective criteria for the assessment of the effect, or lack of effect, of acupuncture on chronic pain as well as to delineate clearly the patient groups and the conditions where acupuncture analgesia is indicated.

screening.rationale: Narrative review that explicitly compared controlled (placebo/sham) and uncontrolled acupuncture trials and discussed placebo response and trial methodology.

classification.summary: Reviewed clinical acupuncture studies for chronic pain, concluded controlled trials showed lower success rates than uncontrolled reports and highlighted the role of placebo response and need for better objective assessment.

title: A critical look at the theory of placebo.

screening.rationale: Title and journal indicate the paper is a conceptual/critical examination of placebo theory, meeting inclusion for placebo science commentary despite no abstract.

classification.summary: Critiques theoretical accounts of the placebo phenomenon and its psychological mechanisms.

title: Placebo: a place in medical therapy?
journal: The Journal of the Kentucky Medical Association

screening.rationale: No abstract or full text available; title suggests a discussion of placebo in therapy but available information is insufficient to confirm inclusion.

classification.summary: Insufficient information in the record to determine methods or results; likely discussed the role of placebos in medical therapy.

title: Comparison of aerosolized atropine, isoproterenol, atropine plus isoproterenol, disodium cromoglycate and placebo in the prevention of exercise-induced asthma.
abstract: In 15 asthmatic children post-exercise bronchospasm was partially inhibited by placebo and by aerosolized atropine sulphate (1 mg) compared with no treatment, not significantly inhibited by atropine alone compared with placebo, partially blocked by disodium cromoglycate (20 mg) and by isoproterenol (0.625 mg) and completely blocked by the combination of isoproterenol and atropine. Pre-treatment with isoproterenol or atropine resulted in post-exercise values for specific conductance which were significantly greater than those following disodium cromoglycate by virtue of the bronchodilator effect of these drugs independent of or in addition to any specific inhibition of exercise-induced asthma. These results suggest that the bronchoconstrictor response to exercise is partially influenced by suggestion but is influenced to a significantly greater degree by mediator release and beta-adrenergic mechanisms and that bronchodilator drugs have therapeutic advantages over an inhibitor of mediator release in the prevention of exercise-induced asthma.

screening.rationale: Randomized/controlled clinical trial that explicitly compared placebo versus no treatment and reported a partial placebo inhibition of post-exercise bronchospasm.

classification.summary: Reported that in 15 asthmatic children aerosolized placebo partially inhibited post-exercise bronchospasm compared with no treatment, while active bronchodilators produced greater inhibition.
classification.key_finding: Placebo aerosol produced partial inhibition of exercise-induced bronchospasm versus no treatment; active bronchodilators (isoproterenol ± atropine) produced larger effects.

title: A comparison of hypnosis, acupuncture, morphine, valium, aspirin, and placebo in the management of experimentally induced pain.
journal: Annals of the New York Academy of Sciences

screening.rationale: Title indicates a multi-arm trial including a placebo arm for experimentally induced pain, but no abstract/full text is available to determine whether the placebo/placebo response was analyzed as an object of study rather than merely a control.

classification.summary: No abstract available; reported a comparative trial of hypnosis, acupuncture, morphine, diazepam, aspirin, and placebo for experimentally induced pain published in 1977.

title: The powerful placebo.
journal: The New York journal of dentistry

screening.rationale: Classic 1955 JAMA paper that is a substantive historical/conceptual review of placebo effects/placebo response in clinical trials, meeting inclusion for placebo science.

classification.summary: Reviews historical clinical trial reports and argued that placebo treatments produced substantial apparent clinical improvement across conditions.
classification.key_finding: Claimed that a sizeable proportion of clinical improvement in trials could be attributed to placebo responses (often cited as ~30%).

title: Placebos: a brief review for family physicians.
abstract: Placebos are as old as the practice of medicine and for thousands of years represented nearly the totality of medical therapeutics. Positive and negative placebo effects occur in about 35 percent and 10 percent of individuals, respectively. Without exception, all medical therapeutics may be assumed to have significant placebo components. Factors contributing to the success of placebos are many, but include the expectations of physician and patient, the doctor-patient relationship, and societal norms. Ethical issues regarding the use of placebos are not clear-cut but, in general, the use of placebos is contraindicated except as an adjunct to specific therapy, or as a research tool with informed consent.

screening.rationale: Narrative review whose main subject is placebo history, prevalence, mechanisms, and ethics, so it meets the 'placebo science' inclusion criterion.

classification.summary: Reviews historical, clinical, and ethical aspects of placebos for family physicians, noting estimated positive and negative placebo rates and roles of expectations and the doctor–patient relationship.
classification.key_finding: Reported roughly 35% positive placebo effects and 10% negative (nocebo) effects, and recommended limited clinical use except with informed consent or as research.

title: Effect of alcohol and benzodiazepines on performance as related to personality characteristics. Personality characteristics among healthy "placebo reactors" and nonreactors.
abstract: For 2 weeks 40 volunteers received either 5 mg diazepam, t.i.d., or 10 mg chlordiazepoxide, t.i.d., and placebo. A choice reaction test, two coordination tests, and an attention test were administered to the subjects on the 14th day of each treatment. Thirty minutes before the tests, the subjects ingested either alcohol., 5g/kg or a placebo drink, incombination with the last capsule. After the test the subjects rated the quality of their treatment as placebo, tranquilizer, or stimulant. The psychological tests taken before the treatments were Eysenck's EPIC-NESI, Taylor's Manifest Anxiety Scale (MAS), and Cattell's 16 PF inventory. A multiple regression analysis was computed. Personality factor scores found to be associated with a strong effect of the benzodiazepines were 16 PF's A, C, L, N, and Q, and EPIC's E. The effect of alcohol was associated with a high score of 16 PFs B factor. Personality factors associated with "placebo reactors" and nonreactors were investigated, as well. Those subjects on placebo indicating their treatment to be active were classified as "placebo reactors". A discriminant analysis revealed that 16PF's O and I factors discriminated effectively "placebo reactors" from nonreactors, and EPIC's SE and 16 PF's L factor nonreactors from "reactors".

screening.rationale: Empirical clinical trial that analyzed personality predictors of 'placebo reactors' (subjects on placebo who reported active effects), so placebo response was an object of study.

classification.summary: Studied 40 healthy volunteers receiving benzodiazepine or placebo (and alcohol or placebo drink) and found personality factors that discriminated subjects who reported active effects while on placebo.
classification.key_finding: Personality (16PF and EPIC factors) distinguished 'placebo reactors' from nonreactors.

title: Patients' attitudes and attributions to electroconvulsive shock therapy.
abstract: An attributional analysis of ECT as a placebo was investigated by comparing the attitudes of patients on two psychiatric wards. It was hypothesized that on the ward on which ECT was administered more frequently, general attitudes toward the treatment would be more favorable and more patients would express the opinion that ECT had worked well for them personally. The results, which supported the predictions, indicate that the operation of placebo effects in connection with ECT may account for differential treatment results more adequately than explanations based on physiological models. The findings also suggest that more research is needed to explore the relationship between patients' attitudes and treatment outcomes.

screening.rationale: Empirical comparative study that investigated ECT as a placebo by comparing patient attitudes and attributions across wards, addressing placebo-related mechanisms/attribution.

classification.summary: Compared patient attitudes on two psychiatric wards and found patients on the ward with more frequent ECT reported more favorable attitudes and greater perceived effectiveness, suggesting placebo/attributional influences on outcomes.
classification.key_finding: Found that higher local exposure to ECT was associated with more favorable attitudes and greater self-reported treatment success, implicating placebo/attribution effects.

title: Placebo versus allopurinol for renal calculi.
abstract: Certain patients with recurrent calcium oxalate calculi will show a mild uricacidemia and/or uricosuria. A prospective blind study was begun in 1970, comparing placebo to allopurinol in the management of these patients. The 92 patients had been followed for a minimum of 6 months to 5 years before the code was broken. It is demonstrated clearly that there is a placebo effect in the management of renal calculous disease. It also has been shown that the only event that clearly separates the 2 groups is complete cessation of calculous formation. Allopurinol is effective in 61 per cent of the patients and these successes usually can be identified after 1 year of treatment.

screening.rationale: Randomized double-blind trial explicitly reported and analyzed a placebo effect in management of recurrent calcium oxalate renal calculi, so placebo response/effect was a focus rather than placebo serving only as comparator.

classification.summary: Randomized blind trial compared allopurinol to placebo in 92 patients with recurrent calcium oxalate stones and reported a clear placebo effect; allopurinol produced cessation of stone formation in 61% of patients.
classification.key_finding: Allopurinol was effective in 61% of patients; the study also reported a measurable placebo effect in management of renal calculi.

title: Gastric and duodenal ulcer healing under placebo treatment.
abstract: The healing time relation of 30 gastric and 15 duodenal ulcers was assessed by repeated endoscopic measurements of ulcer size on days 1, 21, and 42 of a 6-week period, during which a selected population of patients was being treated as outpatients on an inert placebo. Antacids in small amounts were only given in case of ulcer pain. There was evidence for a linear relationship between the absolute initial ulcer size and its reduction with the time in incompletely healed ulcers of both types. Their percentage reduction from the original size was 71% after 3 weeks in gastric and 83% in duodenal ulcers; 82% after 6 weeks in gastric and 83% in duodenal ulcers. The healing time course for both types of ulcers appeared to follow an exponential function. The calculated half-life was 1.7 weeks for gastric and 1.9 weeks for duodenal ulcers. The number of healed duodenal ulcers observed at the 3-week examination was significantly greater than that of healed gastric ulcers (P = 0.05). It is concluded that repeated measurements of the ulcer size before complete ulcer healing contribute to a optimal characterization of the healing time course. The calculated half-life of less than 2 weeks makes shorter control intervals reasonable for both types of ulcers. The ulcer half-life appears to be a more accurate criterion of the healing process than that of complete healing.

screening.rationale: Single-group outpatient study administering an inert placebo and quantifying ulcer healing over time addresses placebo response (within-arm change) rather than using placebo merely as a comparator.

classification.summary: Studied healing time course of 30 gastric and 15 duodenal ulcers in outpatients given an inert placebo, finding marked reductions in ulcer size and estimated half-lives under placebo treatment.
classification.key_finding: Placebo-treated ulcers showed mean percentage reductions of ~71% (gastric) and 83% (duodenal) at 3 weeks, with calculated half-lives of 1.7 weeks (gastric) and 1.9 weeks (duodenal).

title: Comparison of oxyphenbutazone and placebo in the treatment of superficial thrombophelbitis: an object lesson in clinical trial design.

screening.rationale: Title indicates a randomized trial comparing oxyphenbutazone with placebo but no abstract or details to show whether the paper examined placebo/placebo-response as an object of study rather than serving only as a control for drug efficacy.

classification.summary: No abstract available; reported a randomized controlled comparison of oxyphenbutazone versus placebo for superficial thrombophlebitis in 1977, unclear whether placebo effects or responses were analyzed.

title: A double-blind cross-over study: apomorphine/placebo in chronic alcoholics.
journal: International journal of clinical pharmacology and biopharmacy

screening.rationale: No abstract available and title indicates a double-blind crossover trial of apomorphine versus placebo in chronic alcoholics, so it's unclear whether placebo/nocebo effects or placebo-arm analyses were a focus.

classification.summary: No abstract available; reported as a 1977 double-blind crossover trial comparing apomorphine with placebo in chronic alcoholics, with placebo role unclear.

title: Placebo and its importance in medicine.
journal: International journal of clinical pharmacology and biopharmacy
abstract: Placebo can be defined as "a therapeutic effect, drug or non-drug, or a part of it which, in the condition being treated, objectively does not have any specific pharmacodynamic action." Even today when powerful drugs are available placebo is important and present in therapy. Effective therapeutic agents are also sometimes used as placebo, mostly inadvertently. In clinical pharmacological investigations placebos are used deliberately to discriminate the pharmacodynamic action of drugs from psychic and other factors which can influence the objective of the drug evalution. The use of placebo in therapeutic trials is justified only when no effective treatment is available or the symptom or disease is trivial. Placebo effect is especially pronounced in diseases where pain is an important symptom as well as in psychosomatic diseases. The extent of placebo reaction depends on patient's characteristics (reactors and non-reactors), drug presentation, as well as on personality and attitudes of the prescriber. Deliberate use of placebo other than in clinical therapeutic investigation is justified in mild mental depression and in situations where the diagnosis is known, no drug is necessary, but the patient's pressure to get a prescription is irresistible (?). Every doctor should cultivate the induction of placebo reaction in treatment of his patient, but not to the extent that the belief of the former in the action of an inactive medication starts.

screening.rationale: Narrative article whose main subject is the placebo concept, ethics, and clinical use rather than serving as a comparator in a drug efficacy trial, meeting inclusion for placebo science broader topics.

classification.summary: Reviewed the placebo concept, ethical considerations, clinical importance, and determinants (patient traits, drug presentation, prescriber attitudes) and argued for cautious use of placebo responses in mild conditions.

title: Fluphenazine decanoate, oral fluphenazine, and placebo in the treatment of remitted schizophrenics. II. Rating scale data [proceedings].

screening.rationale: Title indicates an RCT comparing fluphenazine formulations with placebo in remitted schizophrenia, but no abstract or full text is available to judge whether placebo/nocebo effects or placebo-arm analyses were a substantive focus.

classification.summary: Reported a controlled trial comparing fluphenazine decanoate, oral fluphenazine, and placebo in remitted schizophrenia, but no abstract was available so focus on placebo effects/analyses could not be determined.

title: Oestrogen therapy and the menopausal syndrome.
abstract: Sixty-four patients with severe menopausal symptoms completed a four month double-blind placebo trial with conjugated equine oestrogens (premarin). Using a graphic rating scale system of assessment, a statistically significant improvement with premarin was observed in 12 psychological and symptomatic scores (Table 3). From a comparison between these results and the results of the 20 patients without vasomotor symptoms it would appear that many of these symptomatic improvements result from the relief of hot flushes (i.e. a domino effect). However, the improvement in memory and reduction of anxiety in these 20 patients suggest that oestrogens have a direct tonic effect on the mental state which is independent of vasomotor symptoms. Sixty-one patients with less severe menopausal symptoms completed the second twelve month double-blind placebo trial and, as assessed by graphic rating scales, a significant improvement with premarin was observed in five psychological and symptomatic scores (Table 3). In both the twelve and four month studies the marked placebo effect of "youthful skin appearance", and on skin greasiness in the twelve month study, indicate that no reliance can be placed on patient judgement of skin texture and appearance. Despite the lessening of the domino effect there was a slight improvement with premarin over placebo in 15 of the remaining 16 symptoms and it is likely that the cumulative effect of these small improvements results in an overall enhancement of well-being. The relief of atrophic vaginitis by premarin did not result in an improvement in libido and this suggests that the ability and the desire to have sexual intercourse are not related. The strength and duration of the placebo effect were well demonstrated in the three standard psychiatric scoring systems, the Beck score (for depression), the General Health Questionnaire and the Eysenck Personality Index (formula: see text) (for neuroticism). We observed a highly significant placebo effect extending for six months in all three, the improvement with premarin over placebo being non-significant. We must conclude that these tests are not sufficiently sensitive to assess psychological or symptomatic changes in menopausal women and that these changes are best assessed by the graphic rating scales. The number of side-effects and complications was assessed in the 61 patients in the long study. A higher incidence of minor side-effects was observed during premarin therapy; this was most marked in relation to leg cramps but radio-isotope scanning revealed no evidence of leg vein thrombosis in these patients or indeed in any patient in the study. Premarin caused no elevation of systolic or diastolic blood pressure; indeed there was a progressive fall in blood pressure throughout the study with no significant difference between premarin and placebo...

screening.rationale: Randomized double-blind placebo-controlled trials reported and explicitly analyzed substantial placebo responses (noting marked placebo effects and their duration), so the paper studies placebo responses.

classification.summary: Conducted two double-blind placebo-controlled trials of conjugated estrogens in menopausal women and found significant drug effects on several symptoms but also marked and sustained placebo responses on multiple subjective measures.
classification.key_finding: Found a highly significant placebo effect on psychiatric scoring systems lasting up to six months, while premarin produced additional symptom improvements on graphic rating scales but not significant advantages on some psychiatric scales.

title: Relaxation training and attention placebo in the treatment of severe insomnia.
journal: Journal of consulting and clinical psychology

screening.rationale: No abstract or full text provided; title indicates an RCT comparing relaxation to an attention placebo but it's unclear whether the paper analyzed placebo/placebo-response as an object of study versus serving only as a control.

classification.summary: Insufficient information to determine whether the attention-placebo was analyzed as an object of study versus serving only as a control in this 1977 randomized trial of relaxation for severe insomnia.

title: A clinical study of the use of human chorionic gonadotrophin in weight reduction.
abstract: Treatment of obesity with human chorionic gonadotrophin was shown to be of no better value than saline in a double-blind crossover study of weight reduction in obese subjects. There was also no significant difference in mood, hunger, or missed injections, and no apparent difference in adherence to diet when the two agents were compared. In contrast, a significant difference was found in the ability of subjects to lose weight in the first four weeks of the study in contrast with the second four weeks, no matter which agent was used. Thus, the initiation of a new therapeutic program, even using an inert agent, has a temporary benefit--a manifestation both of placebo effect and the Hawthorne effect.

screening.rationale: Double-blind crossover trial explicitly analyzed and reported a transient weight-loss benefit regardless of treatment, interpreting this as a placebo/Hawthorne effect (placebo response).

classification.summary: Found hCG was no better than saline in a double-blind crossover obesity trial, with transient weight loss in the first four weeks regardless of agent, interpreted as a placebo/Hawthorne effect.
classification.key_finding: Transient early weight loss occurred irrespective of hCG or saline, indicating a placebo/Hawthorne-related response.

title: A note on the addictive personality: addiction to placebos.

screening.rationale: Case report whose title and publication type indicate the paper focused on compulsive/addictive use of placebos in a clinical patient, meeting inclusion for placebo-science case reports.

classification.summary: Reported a clinical case describing apparent addictive or compulsive use of placebos in an adult female patient with psychiatric comorbidity.
classification.key_finding: Described compulsive consumption of placebo tablets consistent with an 'addiction to placebos' in a psychiatric patient.

title: Temporal effects of drug and placebo in delaying relapse in schizophrenic outpatients.
abstract: The potential for unwanted side effects, particularly tardive dyskinesia, following long-term after care maintenance with antipsychotic medication has led to serious questioning of its continued use for schizophrenic patients. Does the risk of relapse decline with the passage of time? If so, is the advantage of drug therapy sustained and large enough to justify continued treatment beyond one or two years? More appropriate methods for analyzing the after care experience of 374 schizophrenic patients treated with drug or placebo reveals that while the risk of relapse does decline substantially, it remains twice as high for placebo-treated patients than drug-treated patients even after two years of treatment. The prophylactic effect of maintenance chemotherapy appears to be one to two times larger than generally estimated by the less precise "cumulative percentage" method.

screening.rationale: The randomized trial reported and analyzed relapse trajectories separately for drug and placebo arms (placebo-arm outcomes/time course reported), meeting inclusion as placebo response/arm analysis.

classification.summary: Analyzed relapse rates over time in 374 schizophrenic outpatients randomized to chlorpromazine or placebo and found relapse risk declined with time but remained about twice as high in placebo-treated patients after two years.
classification.key_finding: Placebo-treated patients had approximately double the relapse risk of drug-treated patients even after two years.

title: The placebo effect. Is it important in diverticular disease?
abstract: Thirty patients with diverticular disease confirmed by barium enema examination were entered into a three-month double-blind trial of two tablets of methylcellulose (Celevac) daily or two placebo tablets daily. As these tablets were indistinguishable it was possible to cross over nine of the patients and follow them for a further three-month period. The placebo effect was sufficient for 11 patients who completed the trial on placebo to show a small mean improvement. A greater mean clinical improvement was shown, however, by the 16 patients who completed the trial on methylcellulose and in those who were crossed over, most of the improvement occurred during the time the patients were on methylcellulose.

screening.rationale: Randomized double-blind trial explicitly reported and described a placebo-group improvement (placebo response) and compared it with active methylcellulose, so placebo response was a substantive object of analysis.

classification.summary: Randomized double-blind trial in 30 patients with diverticular disease compared methylcellulose versus identical placebo tablets, found a small mean improvement in 11 patients on placebo while greater improvement occurred on methylcellulose.
classification.key_finding: Eleven patients completing the trial on placebo showed a small mean improvement, whereas 16 patients on methylcellulose showed greater mean clinical improvement.

title: Double-blind evaluation of glucagon and propantheline bromide (pro-banthine) for hypotonic duodenography.
abstract: The hypotonic effect of glucagon (2 mg) and propantheline bromide (Pro-Banthine, 30 mg) on the upper gastrointestinal tract was compared in a double-blind study in 12 healthy volunteers and 36 patients. The solvent solution for the two drugs was used as a placebo. Both drugs and placebo were administered intramuscularly. The time of onset of the hypotonic effect was similar for both drugs, with maximum effect achieved 10 min after injection. Effects of glucagon dissapeared rapidly after 30 min, while Pro-Banthine still retained 50% of its maximum effect 2 1/2 hr after injection. Side effects of Pro-banthine were related to the long duration of the hypotonic effect (4-6 hr). A significant placebo effect on the duodenal C loop was observed. Glucagon appears to be the drug of choice since its hypotonic and hypomotile effects on the gastrointestinal tract are comparable to propantheline bromide while having the advantage of shorter duration and practically no side effects.

screening.rationale: Double-blind trial reported and analyzed a significant placebo effect on the duodenal C-loop, so placebo was an object of study rather than only a comparator.

classification.summary: Reported a significant placebo effect on the duodenal C-loop in a double-blind intramuscular comparison of glucagon, propantheline, and solvent placebo in 48 participants; glucagon had shorter duration and fewer side effects.
classification.key_finding: Observed a significant placebo-induced change in duodenal C-loop radiographic appearance; glucagon and propantheline both produced hypotonia versus baseline with differing durations.

title: Differences in placebo effects.
abstract: Constant volume injections of water and saline were evaluated in terms of their effects upon locomotor activity in the rat. Both solutions produced an overall decrease in activity and were found to be nonequivalent in their effect.

screening.rationale: Animal experimental study tested effects of inert injections on locomotor activity in rats, so placebo/contextual effects were the object of study.

classification.summary: Tested effects of constant-volume water and saline injections on rat locomotor activity and found both reduced activity and differed in magnitude.
classification.key_finding: Both water and saline injections produced an overall decrease in locomotor activity, but their effects were nonequivalent.

title: Placebos in psychiatric therapy.

screening.rationale: Title indicates the paper's main subject is placebos in psychiatric therapy (likely a review/commentary) though no abstract is available.

classification.summary: Reviewed the role and implications of placebos in psychiatric therapy, discussing conceptual, clinical, and methodological issues.

title: Treatment of obesity: comparison of physician and nonphysician therapists using placebo and anorectic drugs in a double-blind trial.
abstract: In a randomized double-blind trial, 60 obese patients were assigned in groups of 12 to five therapists. The patients for each therapist were then randomly assigned in groups of four to placebo or one of two preparations of mazindol. Ninety-three percent of the patients completed the nine weeks of treatment. Weight loss averaged 1.1 lb per week and there was no advantage to pharmacological agents over placebo. However, there were significant differences between therapists. Weight loss by the patients assigned to physicians was no better than for those assigned to nonphysician personnel, but there were significant differences between individual nonphysician personnel. These findings support the concept that nonphysician personnel may be effective in treating many obese patients. In addition, we could not find a significant effect of either form of mazindol when compared to placebo.

screening.rationale: Randomized double-blind trial explicitly analyzed placebo (no drug advantage) and therapist/context differences, making placebo response/context a focus.

classification.summary: Randomized double-blind trial in 60 obese adults compared two mazindol preparations and placebo across therapists and found no drug advantage but significant differences in weight loss between therapists.
classification.key_finding: Found weight loss (~1.1 lb/week) across groups with no significant advantage of mazindol over placebo, and significant variation by therapist.

title: Placebo effect of psychotropic drugs on patients and staff.
journal: Revue de neuropsychiatrie infantile et d'hygiene mentale de l'enfance

screening.rationale: Title and publication metadata indicate the paper's stated topic is the placebo effect of psychotropic drugs on patients and staff, meeting inclusion criteria despite no abstract.

classification.summary: Reported on placebo effects of psychotropic drugs on patients and staff; abstract was not available so details of methods and results were not provided.

title: Oral premedication for the problem child: placebo and chloral hydrate.

screening.rationale: No abstract available; title and MeSH indicate a double-blind trial of chloral hydrate versus placebo in pediatric dental premedication, but text does not show whether placebo/nocebo effects or placebo-arm analyses were an object of study.

classification.summary: No abstract available; reported as a double-blind controlled trial comparing oral chloral hydrate versus placebo for pediatric dental premedication.

title: The relative efficacy of methylphenidate (ritalin) and behavior-modification techniques in the treatment of a hyperactive child.
abstract: Drug versus placebo effects were contrasted with those of contingency management in the treatment of a hyperactive child. Several criterion behaviors were monitored in two different settings to gauge the breadth and generalizability of drug and behavior-management effects. Medication and contingency management effects were both found to be situation specific. No interaction effects were found. Accuracy of task performance, amount of eye contact with the experimenters, frequency of repetitive hand movements, and distractible behavior were apparently unaffected by medication (Ritalin versus placebo) within the clinic. A multiple-baseline design incorporating contingency reversals revealed the reinforcement contingencies to be the crucial variable controlling behavior within the clinic. Medication effects were shown to be significant within the home setting where reinforcement contingencies were not changed. While aggressive behavior decreased as a function of Ritalin, repetitive hand movements increased.

screening.rationale: Empirical single-case trial explicitly contrasted drug versus placebo effects and contingency management, so placebo effects/responses were an object of study.

classification.summary: Contrasted Ritalin versus placebo and contingency management in a single hyperactive child using multiple-baseline/reversal, finding situation-specific effects: medication altered some home behaviors but not clinic performance, while contingency management controlled clinic behavior.
classification.key_finding: Medication reduced aggression and affected some home behaviors but did not change clinic task accuracy or eye contact; contingency management drove clinic behavior, and repetitive hand movements increased with Ritalin.

title: Biarison in the treatment of degenerative joint diseases: comparison with indomethacin and placebo.
journal: The Journal of international medical research

screening.rationale: Title and publication types indicate a randomized controlled trial with a placebo arm comparing an active drug, but no abstract or full text is available to determine whether the paper analyzed the placebo/placebo response as an object of study or merely used placebo as comparator.

classification.summary: No abstract available; reported a double-blind clinical trial comparing Biarison, indomethacin, and placebo for degenerative joint disease/osteoarthritis.

title: Fenclofenac in Rheumatoid Arthritis: Sequential Double-blind Cross-over Comparisons with Placebo and Naproxen.
journal: Proceedings of the Royal Society of Medicine

screening.rationale: No abstract/full text provided and title suggests a drug efficacy crossover trial using placebo as a comparator rather than clearly studying placebo/nocebo effects.

classification.summary: No abstract available; title indicated a sequential double-blind crossover trial comparing fenclofenac with placebo and naproxen in rheumatoid arthritis patients.

title: A study of the variations in the response regarding duodenal ulcer when treated with placebo by different investigators.
abstract: Four series of duodenal ulcer patients presenting with pain have been treated with two types of placebos (intramuscular injections or tablets) by 4 different physicians while a fifth group of patients did not receive any treatment. Patients noted the number of days with pain since the beginning of the test by themselves. All patients treated with placebo presented with a significantly shorter duration of pain than untreated patients. There was a significant difference between the actions of the different physicians on the duration of pain. This suggests that some, until now unprecised, character(s) of the physician plays an important part in the relief of duodenal ulcer pain.

screening.rationale: Placebo treatments were compared with a no-treatment group and the study analyzed placebo effects and investigator (physician) differences on pain duration.

classification.summary: Compared placebo injections or tablets versus no treatment in duodenal ulcer patients and found placebo groups had shorter pain duration, with outcomes differing by treating physician.
classification.key_finding: Placebo treatment reduced days with pain compared with no treatment, and relief varied significantly across physicians.

title: A comparative clinical study for the evaluation of antianxiety agents, (lorazepam, diazepam and placebo), in neurosis.
abstract: To evaluate the clinical effects of lorazepam on neurosis, a double-blind controlled trial by group comparison procedure was carried out using diazepam and placebo as control drugs. The clinical improvement and aggravation rates by means of a variety of assessment of change were compared between each of the two active drugs and placebo. The superiority, characteristics of therapeutic effects and minor side effects of lorazepam which is similar to those of diazepam, a standard benzodiazepine anxiolytic for the treatment of neurosis, were demonstrated. From this study, many important problems which might be influenced upon the outcome of the pharmacotherapy on neurotics, such as positive and negative placebo effects, aggravation and drop-out during the trial, were also evaluated.

screening.rationale: Randomized double-blind trial that explicitly compared clinical improvement and evaluated positive and negative placebo effects/aggravation rates rather than using placebo solely as an efficacy comparator.

classification.summary: Conducted a double-blind randomized trial comparing lorazepam, diazepam, and placebo in patients with neurosis and reported therapeutic superiority of lorazepam while evaluating positive and negative placebo effects, aggravation, and drop-outs.
classification.key_finding: Lorazepam showed superior therapeutic effects to placebo and diazepam was similar, while the study documented both positive placebo responses and instances of aggravation/drop-out.
